title: Haematoxylin Eosin (H&E) Staining Protocol
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ihxcb7n
materials: Soaking wax: Because the selected wax melting point is 52~56 ºC, the thermostat is set to 56 ºC, filled with melted wax cup, transparent colon tissue into soft wax cup for 1 hour, then into hard wax dipping wax for another 1 hour;

steps.title: Rinse and fix colon tissue
steps.instruction: Rinse fresh colon tissue with PBS buffer, then immerse in fresh 4 % formalin for 24 h at room temperature, using a volume of fixative 5–10 × the tissue volume to fully cover the sample.

steps.title: Wash fixed tissue
steps.instruction: Rinse the formalin‑fixed colon tissue with a gentle flow of water for 30–60 min to remove residual fixative.

steps.title: Dehydrate tissue through ethanol
steps.instruction: Pass the tissue sequentially through graded ethanol solutions:

substeps.instruction: 100 % ethanol (anhydrous, kept over copper sulfate) – three changes, each 1.5 h

steps.title: Clear tissue with xylene
steps.instruction: Place the dehydrated colon tissue in xylene I (1 : 1 mixture of 100 % ethanol and fresh xylene) for 30 min, then transfer to xylene II (pure fresh xylene) for another 30 min.

steps.title: Embed tissue in paraffin blocks
steps.instruction: Melt hard paraffin wax and pour into an embedding metal box; quickly transfer the cleared tissue into the wax cup using heated forceps, position flat‑bottomed, then place the embedding frame into cold water to solidify, allowing about 20 min for the block to harden. Store the paraffin blocks at room temperature for long‑term use.

steps.title: Trim and section paraffin blocks
steps.instruction: Trim the paraffin blocks as needed and cut sections of 3–10 µm thickness (5 µm is common) using a microtome blade set at a 20–30° angle.

steps.title: Float sections in water bath
steps.instruction: Place the paraffin ribbons in a water bath maintained at 40–45 °C to flatten the sections.

steps.title: Mount sections on slides and dry
steps.instruction: Mount the floated sections onto glass slides, then place the slides on a 60 °C slide warmer for 1–2 h to adhere the sections.

steps.title: Dewax sections in xylene
steps.instruction: Immerse the paraffin sections in xylene I solution for 5 min, then in xylene II solution for another 5 min (use 56 °C in winter if needed).

steps.title: Rehydrate sections through ethanol
steps.instruction: Rehydrate the sections by sequential immersion:

substeps.instruction: Rinse with distilled water for 5 min

steps.title: Stain sections with hematoxylin
steps.instruction: Stain the rehydrated sections in hematoxylin for ~10 min at 30 °C, then rinse with water for 15 min and drain.

steps.title: Differentiate nuclei with HCl ethanol
steps.instruction: Place sections in 1 % hydrochloric acid ethanol differentiation solution for 5–30 s until nuclei turn red, then rinse with water for ~15 min until nuclei appear blue; verify under a microscope.

substeps.instruction: Stain with eosin dye for 2 min
Stain with 0.5 % eosin in alcohol for 1–2 min

steps.title: Clear sections in xylene
steps.instruction: Place sections in xylene I solution for 5 min, then in xylene II solution for 5 min.

steps.title: Apply mounting medium and coverslip
steps.instruction: Remove residual xylene with a paper towel, drip 1–2 drops of neutral Canada gum onto the dry section, gently place a clean coverslip without bubbles using tweezers, and let the slides cure on a paper towel overnight.
